chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
The Ziyārah of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) is equal to twenty Hajjs and is better than twenty Hajjs.
And Muḥammad ibn Ya'qūb narrated to me from a number of his companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, with his chain, similarly.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of performing Ziyarah to Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith to highlight the unique status of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine as a locus of divine grace, where the act of Ziyarah transcends mere physical travel to become a profound spiritual journey. The comparison to twenty Hajj pilgrimages underscores the exceptional reward for visiting the martyr of Karbala, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intercessory and redemptive power associated with the Ahl al-Bayt. This narration serves as a key textual basis for the devotional practice of visiting shrines, elevating it to a status comparable to, and in some interpretations superior to, the obligatory pilgrimage to Mecca.
